note: De-identified. No name, isikukood, or provider identifiers. Source documents remain in Terviseportaal.
staleness_warning: Newest imaging is 2022-03-10; newest clinical contact 2023-11-09. Treat all findings as historical background, not current status.

findings.label: L5 left-sided sacralization with pseudoarthrosis (Bertolotti type)
findings.detail: Pseudoarthrosis between left L5 transverse process and sacrum, with bone marrow oedema at the articulating surfaces. L5/S1 disc space narrowed, osteochondrosis at that level. Serial lumbar MRIs across 2021 also confirmed: no significant disc protrusions or prolapses, spinal canal of uniform width, spinal cord intact, neural foramina not narrowed — nerve root compression is NOT part of this picture.

trajectory.state: more diffuse, spread over wider area

findings.clinical_significance: Considered the main pain generator. Aggravated by lumbar extension combined with rotation and axial load.

findings.label: Minimal right SI subchondral bone oedema
findings.detail: Described as nonspecific, consistent with overload. Joint surfaces even, no erosions, no fusion.
findings.radiologist_recommendation: 2021-01-20 lumbar MRI report explicitly recommended a dedicated SI-joint MRI to clarify possible sacroiliitis. That MRI was carried out 2021-04-26 and found no erosions or joint fusion — a partial structural exclusion, but inflammatory bloodwork (HLA-B27, CRP, ESR) was never done.
findings.open_question: Possible sacroiliitis was explicitly raised 2021-01-20 and structurally ruled out on imaging 2021-04-26, but inflammatory bloodwork was never obtained. See open-questions.json q4.

findings.label: Left acetabular labral lesion, superior-posterior
findings.detail: Cystic formation up to 8 mm with fluid signal, superior-posterior labrum. Alpha angle 47 degrees.
findings.clinical_significance: Location is POSTERIOR; documented symptoms are ANTERIOR (groin). Discordant. May be incidental — labral changes are common in asymptomatic athletes.

findings.label: Right acetabular labral lesion, superior-anterior
findings.detail: 1.2 cm cystic collection, superior labrum slightly anterior to the left-side lesion. Possible additional 3.5 mm cyst on anterior chondral/labral contour. Alpha angle 43 degrees.
findings.clinical_significance: Anterior lesion is on the ASYMPTOMATIC side. Reinforces that labral findings may not be driving symptoms.

findings.label: Suspected left iliopsoas involvement (inferred, not formally diagnosed)
findings.detail: Inference from three consistent findings: anterior groin pain on resisted straight-leg raise (documented 2022-02-02 and 2023-09-20), clicking during the LOWERING phase of hanging leg raises (2020-12-10), and anterior hip joint surface pain location.
findings.clinical_significance: If correct, hip flexor loading is the right target — but as graded tendon loading, not end-range strength work.

findings.label: Minor cam morphology
findings.detail: Small bump at femoral head-neck junction, left greater than right. Alpha angles within normal range (L 47, R 43). Small spindle-shaped calcification at right superior acetabular rim.

findings.label: Right shoulder posterior instability picture (posterior Bankart + SLAP + glenoid dysplasia)
findings.detail: Glenoid flat and dysplastic, approx 30 degrees retroversion. Labrum detached dorsally 12-3 o'clock — a posterior Bankart lesion, as named by the treating physiatrist. Possible old Hill-Sachs lesion. SLAP-type lesion at long head of biceps attachment. Grade III cartilage damage middle third of glenoid. Anterior-superior labrum not distinguishable (detachment or Buford complex). Supraspinatus tendon lower contour slightly uneven (scarring or synovitis), but no rotator cuff tear.
findings.clinical_significance: Three findings together — posterior Bankart, dysplastic retroverted glenoid, possible Hill-Sachs — suggest a prior posterior instability event, not just a SLAP. Limits low-bar back squat rack position and heavy front rack overhead work.

findings.label: Spinoglenoid notch ganglion cyst
findings.detail: 3.3 x 1.3 x 3 cm, in the suprascapular nerve region. No muscle atrophy noted at time of imaging (2022-12).
findings.clinical_significance: Can compress the suprascapular nerve and weaken infraspinatus. Last assessed over 3 years ago. Watch for external rotation weakness or scapular asymmetry.

findings.label: Mild subacromial bursitis, early AC joint arthrosis, humeral osteochondroma
findings.detail: Small subacromial-subdeltoid effusion. Osteochondroma approx 9 x 8 x 13 mm on medial humeral contour. Acromion Bigliani type I. No rotator cuff tear. Subacromial space normal width.

hip_rom.comment: Internal rotation on the low side of normal.

special_tests.rotation_test: Pushing to the LEFT is weaker. Documented 2020-12-10. Consistent with a rotation-based deficit through the left transitional segment.

followups.finding: Pain in groin on resisted straight-leg raise, left. Left SI tender to palpation. Hip ROM free.
Same as above, unchanged. Plus restricted right shoulder movement bringing arm from overhead to behind.

history.mechanism: 3x/week CrossFit plus disc golf competition preparation, loading through the left leg. Named as the trigger in both physiatry notes.
history.mechanism_note: A right-handed backhand drive plants and rotates over the left leg — repeated forceful rotation-extension through a left-sided transitional segment.

working_diagnosis.diagnosis: SI joint irritation and sacralized-vertebra transition-site irritation
working_diagnosis.source: Recorded verbatim in the ortho note the day after the first lumbar MRI. This is the treating clinician's synthesised working diagnosis, distinct from the discrete imaging findings.

symptom_localization_trajectory.2023-09-20: Left hip ANTERIOR surface + low back (localized).
symptom_localization_trajectory.significance: Location description narrowed from broad hip/buttock to anterior hip surface over 3 years. This anterior-surface localization is what reinforces the iliopsoas hypothesis over a labral or SI-primary explanation.

current_functional_asymmetry_2026.reported: 2026-08-06 by user during first session in the app
current_functional_asymmetry_2026.observation: Visible SIDE-HOP / LATERAL SHIFT on ascent from a bilateral back squat. Ascent is not parallel — zig-zags to compensate. Bulgarian split squats also confirmed left side notably weaker, needed more control.
current_functional_asymmetry_2026.clinical_meaning: Active bilateral asymmetry, not just historical. Consistent with the documented left gluteus maximus deficit, left iliopsoas irritability, and left-directional rotation weakness. The 2021 four-month load restriction was followed by no dedicated rehab — six years of compensation habits are now baked into the squat pattern.
programme_priority: Unilateral loading (Bulgarian split squat, single-leg RDL) becomes the highest-value bilateral corrective, not just a supporting movement.
Front squats are corrective for the shift — the bar falls off the rack if the ascent isn't symmetric.
Paused squats at the bottom force even weight distribution.
Consider filming the squat regularly to track visible shift as a KPI, not just weight and reps.
Physiotherapy remains the highest-value unaddressed clinical action — flag this specifically to the physio if/when the appointment happens.

what_worked.note: Orthopaedist recorded positive dynamics on exercise, strength indicators significantly improved. Specific exercises not documented in the record.
what_worked.significance: Objective evidence that loading helped. Argues against treating this as fragile.

load_restriction_period.content: Avoid squat, deadlift, and other movements loading the lower limb and lumbosacral junction.

injections.reason: Orthopedist elected NOT to inject. Reasoning: dominant irritation focus is in BONE (oedema), not the joint capsule. An intra-articular blockade wouldn't address bone-stress. Load modulation prescribed instead.

injections.outcome: Pain substantially relieved, mobility restriction persisted
injections.note: Subacromial injection treats bursitis. Does not address labral or instability pathology — consistent with the partial response.

physiotherapy_engagement.detail: First referral not attended. Second: missed appointment 2023-10-18, one session 2023-11-02 where meaningful mobilization was not possible due to significant muscle guarding. Acupuncture and EMTT given.
physiotherapy_engagement.flag: Highest-value unaddressed action in the entire record.

history.surgical_fallback_mentioned: Lumbosacral fusion or facet resection, if symptoms persist and do not respond to load modulation (2021-04-29).

provocative_positions.label: Deep hip flexion + adduction + internal rotation
provocative_positions.reason: FADIR was positive bilaterally, left worse. Occurs under load when knees cave in a squat.

provocative_positions.label: Loaded end-range hip flexion, especially eccentric
provocative_positions.reason: Clicking documented in the lowering phase of hanging leg raises.

provocative_positions.label: Resisted straight-leg raise, left
provocative_positions.reason: Reproduces groin pain. Documented twice, a year apart.

provocative_positions.label: Heavy axial spinal load (back squat, conventional deadlift)
provocative_positions.reason: The original presenting complaint — could not stand up from a deadlift due to sharp pain.

red_flags.label: Pain that wakes you at night
Sharp catch or click WITH pain in the groin
Deep dull ache in left buttock / SI area lasting over 48h
Pain that shortens your stride when running
New weakness in shoulder external rotation, or scapular asymmetry
red_flags.reason: Possible suprascapular nerve compression from the spinoglenoid cyst.

red_flags.label: Morning stiffness over 30 min, back pain improving with movement and worsening with rest, second-half-of-night waking
red_flags.reason: Inflammatory back pain screen. Never formally excluded.
